It is a close analogue of Li2MgCl4, the lowest-penalty candidate so far. Zn2+ is a hard-to-reduce, fully oxidized cation, though it may be somewhat more reducible than Mg2+, so the penalty could differ.
proposal.motivation: Li2MgCl4 (mp-aaaacffw) gave the lowest penalty so far (0.189 eV/non-Li atom, bin 9). Li3PO4 and LiF, with non-matching anions, gave 0.31-0.34 eV, and the borate and silicate picks gave 0.20-0.72 eV.

proposal.hypothesis: LiCaAlF6 is a wide-gap mixed fluoride built from hard, fully oxidized Ca2+ and Al3+ with no reducible transition metal. Fluorides are generally stable against Li metal and near 4 V. Earlier LiF gave a large penalty, but the stable Ca/Al fluoride framework may reduce the anion-driven and cation-driven metathesis seen with the oxides, chlorides and silicates. This is a mixed-cation fluoride, distinct from the binary LiF and the earlier chloride and oxide picks.
proposal.motivation: Every earlier pick was insulating with a large band gap but had a contact penalty of 0.19 to 0.72 eV/non-Li atom, above the 0.05 eV threshold. The best so far was the chlorides Li2MgCl4 and Li2ZnCl4 at 0.189 eV (bin 9). The fluoride LiF gave 0.31 eV. A multi-cation fluoride is a new variant of the halide family that has not yet been tested.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2SiF6 is a wide-gap fluoride with a fully oxidized, hard Si4+ cation and no reducible transition metal, so it is structurally close to the best candidate, LiCaAlF6. Its Si-F framework should resist sulfide reduction and PF5-type metathesis, which were the main contact products. The single remaining evaluation is best spent on a close fluoride analogue that might lower the 0.048 eV/non-Li penalty further.
proposal.motivation: LiCaAlF6 (mp-aaaaajby) was the only acceptable candidate, with penalty 0.0477 eV/non-Li atom (bin 2). Its contact products were mainly sulfur and PF5-type species. The oxides, chlorides and silicate with other anions were all above 0.19 eV, so the fluoride framework is the most promising family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2TiF6 is a wide-gap fluoride like the best candidate so far, LiCaAlF6, which was the only acceptable pick (penalty 0.048 eV/non-Li atom). Its hard, fully oxidized fluoride framework should resist PF5-type and sulfur-forming metathesis with Li6PS5Cl. Ti4+ is somewhat reducible compared with Ca2+ or Al3+, so the penalty may be higher. It is the closest untested fluoride, and I expect it to behave like the Li2SiF6 analogue (0.081 eV) but with a possibly different Ti-driven reduction term.
proposal.motivation: LiCaAlF6 (mp-aaaaajby) gave the only acceptable penalty (0.0477 eV, bin 2). Li2SiF6 (mp-aaacpxez) gave 0.081 eV (bin 4). Oxides, chlorides, borates and silicates with non-fluoride anions gave penalties of 0.19 to 0.72 eV. The fluoride family is therefore the most promising, and the remaining untested fluorides are Li2TiF6 and LiNbF6.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbF6 is a wide-gap fluoride built on a fully oxidized Nb5+ cation, with no low-valent reducible state. Its fluoride framework should resist the sulfide-driven PF5/S/SCl metathesis that dominated the other fluoride contacts. It is the last untested fluoride on the list and the closest remaining analogue of the best candidate, LiCaAlF6 (0.048 eV, bin 2). The Nb5+ framework may give a lower penalty than the Ti4+ and Si4+ analogues (0.076 and 0.081 eV).
